Vivek,

Thanks for the updated DPA redlines. Two execution logistics items came up in our legal ops standup that we need to lock down before we can countersign: 

1) Escrow acknowledgement: Acme requires a notarized/escrow witness acknowledgement for the Escrow Annex: a named custodian (BrightLedger) must sign as an acknowledgement of custody for encryption keys. We need to confirm Redwood is amenable to an acknowledgement rather than independent escrow of keys.

2) Signatory authority & routing: our legal team wants the signing order to be: Acme Legal -> Acme CFO -> Redwood Countersign (serial). We prefer DocuSign envelope with IDs prefilled and an audit witness stage (not an additional signer, just witness flag).

Can you confirm: (a) whether Redwood will accept an acknowledgement signer (BrightLedger) listed as "Witness (non-executive)" in the envelope, and (b) whether you can disable automatic envelope auto-advance until the witness checkbox is recorded?

Patricia
Acme Corp — Legal

Patricia — thanks, this is clear. Short answers up front: yes to acknowledgement signer; yes we can configure the envelope to pause before final countersign so the witness confirmation is visible in the audit trail. A few details and asks below so we match expectations exactly.

- Witness role (BrightLedger): please provide full legal name, email, and a brief KYC statement so our compliance team can accept the acknowledgement (BrightLedger is a subprocessor in your redline). We typically treat the witness as a "For Acknowledgement" recipient type in DocuSign (no authority to change contract terms).
- Countersign step: Redwood will countersign after the named Redwood sig (VP Legal or Head of Contracts). Who at Acme will be the final approver for the CFO step (name + email)?
- Escrow annex: if you want a notarized acknowledgment beyond a DocuSign witness flag, flag it now — that will change timelines.

I'll loop in Laura (legal) and Rishi (contracts) to confirm authority and the DocuSign template settings (serial routing; disable auto-advance).

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Laura / Rishi — looped in for legal/contract authority: Acme wants an external witness acknowledgement (BrightLedger) included in the DocuSign envelope and for us to disable auto-advance until witness checkbox is recorded. They also propose sign order: Acme Legal -> Acme CFO -> Redwood countersign.

Can you confirm:
- Who is the correct Redwood countersignatory (title/name) for this deal?
- Is an acknowledgement-only recipient acceptable from a compliance standpoint (no execution authority)?

I want to avoid having the envelope auto-complete and then needing to re-open for countersign. Rishi, if we need a canary/countersign template in DocuSign (manual hold), please advise.

—V

Vivek — legal is comfortable with the proposed approach with these constraints: 

1) Witness acknowledgement: accept as "For Acknowledgement" recipient type in DocuSign. We need BrightLedger's KYC statement and an email address we can validate. We will record the acknowledgement text as an exhibit (Escrow Annex) rather than granting any signatory authority.
2) Countersign authority: Redwood countersign must be completed by our Head of Legal (Laura Bennett) or designated deputy. Please cc me on the envelope and use the template variable "require_manual_countersign" so Rishi can block auto-complete.
3) Audit evidence: capture BrightLedger's email and a copy of their KYC (simple attachment). If Acme requires notarization, escalate — we treat notarization as out-of-band and will need 7–10 business days.

Rishi — recommend using serial routing with the "hold for manual signature" flag on the final recipient. DocuSign template ID: TPL-RED-EC-007 (internal). I'll also attach a short Annex draft for the acknowledgement language — see Escrow_Annex_draft.docx.

Laura
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Marissa — please confirm procurement path and whether finance needs to be notified before countersign.
